newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty reports hundreds of killings in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty reports hundreds of killings in Zaire.

text.p: Zairean government forces and rebels have killed hundreds of civilians and refugees in the past few months, Amnesty International said on Thursday.

The London-based human rights organisation said eyewitnesses had told of a series of killings in South Kivu in eastern Zaire, an area that has been cut off from the outside world for the past two months.

"The evidence shows that there has been a systematic and deliberate policy of armed attacks and indiscriminate killings to flush out civilians and refugees, as well as deliberate and arbitrary killings," Amnesty said in a statement.
The organisation's findings were based on interviews with people who had fled from South Kivu to Tanzania.
The witnesses reported that about 100 Tutsis from a Methodist church were massacred by Zairean militia in the villages of Lueba and Mboko in September.
The following month, Tutsi rebels attacked a hospital, killing at least 38 patients and nurses, Amnesty said. Patients too ill to flee from their beds were shot in the head.
About 60 civilians, including babies, were killed by Tutsis in the town of Kiliba on October 18 and a few day's later several people at Luberezi camp were killed, also by Tutsis, the statement said.
Amnesty said Tutsis killed around 300 people in the village of Mboko in late October.

"This face of the Zaire tragedy has so far been hidden from international scrutiny -- and with this area cut off from the outside world there are real fears that the attacks and killings are continuing today," Amnesty said.
The recent problems in eastern Zaire erupted in mid-1996 after Tutsis with historic links to Zaire were denied citizenship and fighting broke between them and Zairean government forces.
More than 600,000 refugees fled to Rwanda but many others went deeper into eastern Zaire and aid agencies are still struggling to reach them.
Amnesty called on the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to mount an independent investigation into attacks on refugee camps.
